subject: Deployment mode and cost modeling follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up + cost model (recap from call)

Alex — thanks again for taking the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps.

Key needs you mentioned:
- Data residency + PHI: must remain in US and behind customer-controlled networking (VPC) for production.
- Latency target: <200ms end-to-end for interactive flows; batch/async can be higher.
- Scale: pilot ~300M tokens/month, ramp to ~1B tokens/month over 12 months if adoption goes well.
- Concurrency: expected peak ~15 qps (90th percentile) for UI traffic.

Deployment paths we discussed:
1) Hosted API — fastest to start (no infra lift). Per-token pricing, simple quotas, Redwood-managed infra. Good for quick PoC but does NOT provide customer VPC or dedicated hardware.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — reserved GPU pool (SLA-backed), predictable throughput, better unit economics at scale via committed monthly fees plus lower per-token rates. Can be isolated per customer.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — full network isolation, customer-managed network/VPC or on-prem appliance. Best for production PHI/regulatory requirements; higher upfront work and typically a platform license + infra.

Attached is a first-pass cost model comparing the three options (redwood-cost-modeling-acmehealth.xlsx). I put in a few scenarios using your pilot (300M tokens/mo) and scale (1B tokens/mo) numbers. Highlights below — these are estimates, we can refine with exact token mix (prompt vs completion) and concurrency profile:  

- Hosted API (estimate):
  • Prompt: $0.03 / 1k tokens  
  • Completion: $0.06 / 1k tokens  
  • Pilot (300M tokens): ~$10.5k/month  
  • Scale (1B tokens): ~$35k/month

- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  • Example commit: $35k/month for a 4-GPU pool (A100 class) with predictable throughput.
  • Effective unit cost depends on utilization; at 1B tokens that maps to ~$0.018 / 1k tokens if utilization is high.
  • Pros: predictable latency, capacity isolation, custom autoscale policies.

- Private VPC / On-prem:
  • Typical structure: one-time onboarding/installation + monthly platform fee + customer infra costs.
  • Example: $50k one-time onboarding, $12k/month platform fee (plus infra). At scale this can be lower unit cost but requires procurement and ops.

Questions / proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm the expected prompt vs completion token split (rough %)? I used 40/60 prompt/completion in the spreadsheet.
2) Do you want us to model a 12-month reserved commit (vs month-to-month) for Dedicated — we can show delta for 6/12/24 month terms.
3) I'll loop in Marissa (solutions) to confirm latency SLA and sizing assumptions — can we schedule a 30m pricing + infra call next week?

Thanks — I’ll wait for the token split and preferred times.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear recap, Aditya — this aligns with our conversation. A few clarifications from our side:

- Data/regulatory: production must be in our VPC (we cannot have PHI leave our network). Pilot could run in a dedicated, customer-isolated environment hosted by Redwood (i.e., Dedicated with VPC peering) until we validate everything.
- Token mix: for the initial pilot expect 30% prompt / 70% completion (longer completions).
- Timeline: pilot start target is mid-April; decision on procurement by end of March.
- Procurement: procurement will want committed pricing and an SOW; we will likely push for a 12-month financial commitment for better unit economics.

A couple questions: what is the minimum committed capacity for Dedicated? And for Private VPC, what level of infra work do you expect on our side vs Redwood? Also can you confirm SOC2 scope and whether Redwood can provide the report for our security review?

If you can update the model using 30/70 split and show a 12-month reserved commit vs month-to-month, that would be great. Happy to do a quick sync with Marissa + procurement next week — Tue/Wed mornings PT work for me.

—Alex
Alex Turner

Alex — thanks, marking 30/70 token split and 12-month commit preference. I updated the attached spreadsheet with three scenarios: Hosted, Dedicated (month-to-month), Dedicated (12-month reserved), and Private VPC. Summary of the updated numbers (30% prompt / 70% completion):

Pilot (300M tokens/mo) — estimates
- Hosted API: ~$12k/month
- Dedicated month-to-month: ~$28k/month (minimum 4-GPU pool)
- Dedicated 12-month reserved: ~$22k/month (prepaid discount applied)
- Private VPC (first year amortized): ~$30k/month (includes onboarding)

Scale (1B tokens/mo) — estimates
- Hosted API: ~$40k/month
- Dedicated 12-month reserved: ~$60k/month (effective unit cost lower with utilization)
- Private VPC (amortized): ~$45k/month + infra

Notes / assumptions:
- These are illustrative — exact numbers depend on model family (larger models increase GPU needs), sequence length, and real-world utilization.
- Dedicated committed pricing assumes a 4-GPU baseline for your latency/concurrency needs; we can size up/down with Marissa.
- Private VPC numbers include a one-time onboarding fee ($50k) amortized over 12 months in the attached sheet. Customer infra cost not included.

Answers to your specific questions:
- Minimum committed capacity for Dedicated: 4 GPUs (typical starting point) — we can provide partial burst capacity but baseline commit starts there.
- Private VPC infra split: Redwood handles the platform, deployment, and runtime; customer provides VPC peering, subnets, and any on-prem hardware (if choosing on-prem). We provide an install/run SOW.
- SOC2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II — I’ve attached the standard SOC 2 attestation link and will have Marissa send the security pack.

Next steps I propose:
1) 30m pricing & infra review — Tue 03/03 9:30am PT or Wed 03/04 10:00am PT. Please confirm which works.
2) If procurement wants a draft SOW and 12-month quote, we can surface a redline-ready SOW (attached SOW-draft-AcmeHealth.pdf).
3) Marissa will follow up on sizing/latency assumptions.

Alex — quick technical notes from the sizing perspective:

- For the latency target (<200ms) and 15 qps peak with a 30/70 split, a 4-GPU A100-class pool is our baseline for Dedicated. That assumes sequence lengths similar to the samples you shared (avg completion ~250 tokens).
- If you expect longer completions consistently (>= 500 tokens), we should consider 6 GPUs to avoid increased queuing. I added alternate rows in the workbook.
- SOC2 artifacts: we can deliver the attestation and a security pack within 3 business days; for deeper controls testing we can coordinate a security review call.
- For Private VPC: typical onboarding (30–45 days) and we provide a runbook + automated deployment scripts. We will need a brief network assessment call to confirm subnets and egress rules.
